page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the Enhanced c7nex family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, along with cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. In performance tests, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 154.46 GB/sec with write throughput at 67.93 GB/sec. The instance includes a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not provision bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external networked block storage for persistent filesystem configurations.

Standardized benchmark evaluations place the system firmly within the median performance bracket for its hardware class. The host achieved a multi-core stress-ng rating of 31066.87, a multi-core Geekbench score of 13816.0, and a PassMark CPU aggregate score of 36747.88. Key workload metrics demonstrate 31.02 million operations per second during Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 32.08 GB/sec.

Given its 40 Gbps network pipe and compute-focused vCPU density, the ecs.c7nex.8xlarge offers balanced operational efficiency for parallel processing without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity. Workload fit includes high-throughput web serving, software build clusters, cryptographic microservices, network appliances, and CPU-bound batch processing jobs.
